**8B.9 Research Note: Sheikh Hasina in 2024**

**Bottom line:** Mostly no. There is real evidence that Hasina’s government used some tools to preserve regime objectives and capacity, especially in macro stabilization, procurement digitization, and a few diplomatic / technical domains. But the decisive 2024 pattern was coercive crisis management, election control, information suppression, and failure to contain the July protest crisis. That looks more like regime-defense that ultimately collapsed than durable, adaptive preservation of regime influence.

**Accepted claims**
- **Bangladesh IMF review says corrective macro steps were underway** | IMF | June 24, 2024 | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/06/24/pr24234-bangladesh-imf-exec-board-concludes-2nd-review-ecf-eff-rsf | The IMF said Bangladesh had already realigned the exchange rate, adopted a crawling peg, tightened monetary policy, and advanced tax/subsidy reforms. This is the strongest evidence that the regime adjusted methods to protect macro stability and keep the state functioning. **QIDs:** 8B.9, 8B.8
- **Mandatory e-procurement reform** | Bangladesh Public Procurement Authority | March 6, 2024 | https://bppa.gov.bd/media-communication/news-1446.html | BPPA said online procurement was mandatory, with broad agency registration and improved transparency, efficiency, and competition. This suggests the regime was strengthening an administrative instrument to reduce leakage and keep state capacity usable. **QIDs:** 8B.9, 8B.8
- **Whole-of-government Smart Bangladesh rollout** | UNB | June 4, 2024 | https://www.unb.com.bd/category/Bangladesh/govt-adopts-plan-to-turn-public-welfare-services-into-smart-services-in-two-years/136812 | The government moved 52 ministries and divisions into a Smart Bangladesh implementation platform. That is evidence of regime coordination and administrative mobilization to keep the governing program moving. **QIDs:** 8B.9, 8B.8
- **Planning Commission embeds Smart Bangladesh into the Five Year Plan** | Dhaka Tribune | April 16, 2024 | https://www.dhakatribune.com/amp/bangladesh/344095/official-document-govt-to-include-smart | Planning authorities sought to turn Smart Bangladesh into formal planning targets for macro stability, jobs, poverty reduction, and rule of law. This shows adaptation through institutionalization of the regime’s chosen agenda. **QIDs:** 8B.9, 8B.8
- **Rohingya policy handled through diplomacy and border control** | TBS News / UNB | July 10, 2024 | https://www.tbsnews.net/bangladesh/pm-hasina-reiterates-call-china-help-repatriate-rohingyas-myanmar | Hasina pushed Rohingya repatriation through talks with Myanmar and support from China. That is a case of using diplomatic channels to preserve a security objective rather than relying only on force. **QIDs:** 8B.9
- **Nuclear posture stayed restrained and institutional** | Dhaka Tribune | April 30, 2024 | https://www.dhakatribune.com/bangladesh/foreign-affairs/345281/bangladesh-reaffirms-commitment-to-nuclear-non-proliferation-peaceful-use | Bangladesh said it would maintain transparency, safety, and IAEA-backed safeguards for nuclear plants. This is narrow, but it supports the view that the regime protected influence through disciplined institutional management rather than reckless escalation. **QIDs:** 8B.9

**Negative / stronger claims**
- **Refusal to empower a neutral election authority** | Reuters | January 4, 2024 | https://theprint.in/world/little-election-fizz-in-bangladesh-as-prime-minister-set-for-another-term/1910693/ | Reuters reported the opposition boycott followed Hasina’s refusal to resign and allow a neutral authority to run the election. This shows regime durability was being pursued by controlling the electoral apparatus, not by opening contestation. **QIDs:** 8B.9
- **Election designed to keep Hasina in power** | Reuters | January 7, 2024 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-turnout-low-in-election-set-to-keep-pm-hasina-in-power-3268699 | Reuters described the contest as one set to keep Hasina in power rather than a genuinely competitive election. This is direct evidence of regime-preservation behavior. **QIDs:** 8B.9
- **July crisis escalated through curfew, troop deployment, and shutdowns** | Reuters | July 20, 2024 | https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-army-enforces-curfew-as-student-led-protests-spiral/2182818/ | Reuters reported soldiers, roadblocks, and internet/text shutdowns as the protest crisis escalated. This is coercive regime defense, not successful crisis management. **QIDs:** 8B.9
- **Hasina doubled down instead of compromising** | Reuters | July 22, 2024 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-pm-hasina-blames-opposition-for-violence-curfew-to-remain-3528153 | Hasina kept the curfew in place and blamed political opponents for the violence. That is strong evidence of blame-shifting and refusal to pivot to de-escalation. **QIDs:** 8B.9
- **UN said the crackdown increased impunity** | UN OHCHR | July 26, 2024 | https://bangladesh.un.org/en/275065-bangladesh-t%C3%BCrk-decries-government-crackdown-urges-respect-international-human-rights | The UN said more than 170 people had been killed and that internet shutdowns increase impunity. That strongly undercuts any claim that Hasina preserved regime durability through lawful, effective control. **QIDs:** 8B.9
- **Army refusal shows coercive plan failed, not that the ruler adapted** | Reuters / VOA | August 7, 2024 | https://www.voanews.com/a/exclusive-bangladesh-army-refused-to-suppress-protest-sealing-hasina-s-fate/7733166.html | Reuters reported the army would not fire on civilians to enforce Hasina’s curfew. This suggests her chosen coercive method failed because implementers would not comply, and I found no evidence she then successfully adjusted course. **QIDs:** 8B.9, 8B.8
- **HRW says the crackdown was the deadliest in recent Bangladesh history** | Human Rights Watch | August 26, 2024 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/26/bangladesh-back-un-investigation-grave-abuses | HRW said the crackdown killed at least 440 people, with excessive force by law enforcement and Awami League-linked youth violence. This is strong evidence that the regime failed to manage opposition and institutional resistance in a way that preserved legitimacy or durability. **QIDs:** 8B.9
- **Late-2024 macro and growth outcomes still deteriorated** | Reuters | August 8, 2024 | https://m.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/factboxtroubled-bangladeshs-economy-bogged-down-by-high-unemployment-inflation-3561503?ampMode=1 | Reuters summarized widening external deficits, taka depreciation, falling reserves, IMF dependence, and stagnant job creation. Even where the regime tried to adjust, the broader stewardship outcome was not stable or durable. **QIDs:** 8B.9, 8B.8
- **Crony capitalism and elite capture remained the operating pattern** | The Daily Star | October 31, 2024 | https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/al-govt-created-lawless-economy-3741796 | A white-paper lead said authoritarian practices produced crony capitalism and a nexus of bureaucrats, political leaders, and business interests that captured public organizations. This is direct evidence against durable, disciplined regime management through competent institutions. **QIDs:** 8B.9

**Search gap**
- I did not find strong evidence of a successful mid-2024 reset that preserved regime stability after the quota protests began.
- The best positive evidence is sector-specific or externally pressured, while the strongest domestic-crisis evidence points to coercion, not adaptive preservation.
- I also did not find a clear, documented replacement of failed security or political implementers before the regime collapsed.

**Overall assessment for 8B.9:** Hasina sometimes used technocratic and diplomatic tools to protect regime objectives, but in the decisive 2024 political crisis she relied on coercion, censorship, and blame-shifting. That failed to preserve regime durability or influence.
